question.:question/problem: If $c=[\begin{aligned}k \\ 3k \\ -6\end{aligned}],$ $d=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 3 \\ 3\end{aligned}],$ and $c⊥d,$ then $k=${{field-1}}.
question.:question/worked-solution:
We know that $c⊥d$ ($c$ and $d$ are perpendicular) if and only if $c\cdot d=0.$

Computing the dot product, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}c\cdot d & ={c}_{x}\cdot {d}_{x}+{c}_{y}\cdot {d}_{y}+{c}_{z}\cdot {d}_{z} \\  & =k\cdot 3+3k\cdot 3+(-6)\cdot 3 \\  & =3k+9k-18 \\  & =12k-18.\end{aligned}
$$

Setting the dot product equal to $0,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}c\cdot d & =0 \\ 12k-18 & =0 \\ k & =\frac{3}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
